name: Understanding why the model predicts
gist: Making time series models interpretable and explainable—showing which past values matter, why anomalies occur, or what causal patterns the model has found.
explain: A model that forecasts accurately is valuable, but a model that also explains itself is priceless. A hospital wants to know: which vital signs led the model to predict a crisis, because doctors need to understand the clinical reasoning. A factory wants to know: why did the model flag this sensor reading as anomalous, because maintenance engineers need to know if the flagging is real or a false alarm. A trader wants to know: did the model's price prediction come from technical patterns or fundamental data, because the trading strategy depends on the underlying logic. Understanding the model's reasoning builds trust because humans can verify that the model is using real patterns and allows verification that the model is learning sensible patterns, not spurious correlations created by the training data. It also enables debugging because if the model is wrong, seeing what it focused on helps identify where the prediction went astray.

Interpretability for sequences is tricky because sequences have temporal structure. A black-box neural network processes information through many layers, and by the end, the signal is transformed beyond recognition. Traditional linear models are transparent—each coefficient shows the contribution of one variable. But linear models are often too weak for complex sequences. The question is how to get both expressiveness and explainability. Some papers use attention mechanisms, which show which past time steps the model attends to. Others use saliency maps, which highlight which input values most influence the output. A few papers build interpretable architectures from the ground up, sacrificing some accuracy to maintain clarity.

Papers in this theme focus on making sequence models transparent. Some extract rules from neural models—for example, 'if the past three values are increasing and the growth rate accelerates, predict a peak.' Others use methods to identify which past values truly drive the future, rather than just correlating with it. Some combine neural and symbolic approaches: let the neural network be flexible, but require it to produce outputs that are human-interpretable or satisfy domain constraints. The underlying principle is that in high-stakes domains like healthcare or infrastructure, a slightly less accurate but fully explainable model is often preferred to a black-box model with marginal accuracy gains.

papers.title: Exposing Vulnerabilities in Explanation for Time Series Classifiers via Dual-Target Attacks
papers.contribution: Reveals that explanation stability is a misleading proxy for robustness, motivating coupling-aware robustness evaluation.

papers.title: ProSAR: Prototype-Guided Semantic Augmentation and Refinement for Time Series Contrastive Learning
papers.contribution: Demonstrates improved representation learning across time-series benchmarks with explicit semantic guidance and feedback-based prototype refinement.

papers.title: ProtoTS: Learning Hierarchical Prototypes for Explainable Time Series Forecasting
papers.contribution: ProtoTS exceeds existing methods in forecast accuracy while delivering expert-steerable interpretations for better model understanding, released with source code.

papers.title: TopoDistill: Distilling Global System Topology for Causal Discovery in Multivariate Time Series
papers.contribution: Improves causal discovery in multivariate time series by maintaining specificity against spurious correlations while enabling effective identification under noise.

papers.title: TimeSAE: Causal Sparse Decoding for Faithful Explanations of Black-Box Time Series Models
papers.contribution: Provides more faithful and robust explanations than leading baselines on both synthetic and real-world time series datasets.

papers.title: Words Towards Explainability: Caption Label-Free Learning via Dual Loop Agentic Time Series Captioning
papers.contribution: Achieves caption generation without label supervision via exploration-feedback mechanism and releases TFTSC, an industrial expert-level time series caption dataset.
